Hi everyone

Hey Hassan, what kind of security incidents do you want to investigate on?

The common tools like Splunk, Tenable, etc. got ai-powered or ai-driven solutions. But I bet thats not what you would expect from AI.
They can identify anomalies across multiple systems on a huge data base or automatically generate reports for audits quite well. But they cannot detect and respond or fix threats in a way that it could replace an expert or fully automate parts of the incident handling process. They can actually support you and accelerate your work and give you quite good hints where to keep an eye on. 

Tools like appdynamics, datadog, splunk or new relic are often related to AIOps and suggest to you that this is the solution you are looking for. But instead you should have a look at the complete SDLC and focus on the origin of the risks. Build a DevSecOps pipeline which covers the development and the operation of the code/software which you operate or try to protect. Don’t let security be an afterthought. 

- Copilot can support you in checking your code 
- Veracode helps you identify and fix your code (SAST, DAST, SCA)
- Snyk covers the SAST part 
- tenable takes the vulnerability management part 
- and the tools mentioned at the beginning are usually monitoring tools at the end of the Pipeline / Lifecycle.

Try to cover all aspects and focus on a shift-left security strategy to reduce the noise at the end.
For live testing of the network, Insight VM and Shodan are best
These tools can help identify and report vulns on the go

Oops - Crowdstrike just demonstrated a serious vulnerability - directly internet-connected critical systems are updated with neither testing nor a backout plan...
Of course all those third party sw vendors have equally rigorous protection 🙂

Thats not exactly a vulnerability though. Its a bug in an update they pushed out that bricked many Windows machines with the software installed. 

A vulnerability is more so a backdoor or issue that allows security threats like remote access, priviledge escelation, etc that is present in functioning software/systems.

The point of reporting and tracking vulns is that something is found in a healthy system that allows undesired behavior that you are not aware of. 

This situation with Crowdstrike rendered systems unoperable and was an update pushed out. Its not like a malignant cancer cell in the body you should get removed. More like you ate food that was genetically altered and now you are sick and having a reaction that was not previously occurring(think peanuts and what was done to gluten in wheat strains).

I would agree though that if we used the term "vulnerability" very loosely then we could apply it to the process of how they interact with their customers machines but again, not really the reason for this channel and thats a loose application.

Also it is more so the customers who are choosing to use Windows and software that can update at such a low-level for quick security rather than creating a network that is secure. And weve seen for decades now how Windows/Microsoft products behave. 

Its only going to get worse from here.

Most of the companies impacted are actually only having issues at the POS or terminal stations. So they use Linux/BSD for servers and whatnot but at the train station or local bank branch office they are using Windows and those machines are impacted. 

Its an easy fix; migrate away from Microsoft and stop assuming your employees are so non-tech orientated that they must use Windows and cannot learn Fedora or Debian.

It baffles me when I see a dumb TV used for showing a webpage that provides information like a menu at a resturant or perhaps flight times at an airport connected to a computer using Windows...such a waste and a Raspberry Pi would be very ideal in those scenarios.

This is a show of just how lazy some people have become even in our most precious systems in society. Windows PE(or full blown Windows 11) on an Intel NUC when Debian(which is free) on a Raspberry Pi would be for more suitable

Looks like I was wrong about this being about Windows and Linux behavior however, most Admins that use Linux would not use something like what Crowdstrike provides. 

Issues were reported months ago about Crowdstrike software causing boot issues in Debian.
